panels.label: Steering
panels.description: Lateral control, lane changes, and steering behavior

items.title: Enable Modular Assistive Driving System (MADS)
items.description: Enable MADS. Disable toggle to revert back to stock sunnypilot engagement/disengagement.

items.title: Toggle with Main Cruise
items.description: Note: For vehicles without LFA/LKAS button, disabling this will prevent lateral control engagement.

items.title: Unified Engagement Mode (UEM)
items.description: Engage lateral and longitudinal control with cruise control engagement. Note: Once lateral control is engaged via UEM, it will remain engaged until it is manually disabled via the MADS button or car shut off.

items.title: Steering Mode on Brake Pedal
items.description: Choose how Automatic Lane Centering (ALC) behaves after the brake pedal is manually pressed in sunnypilot.

sections.title: Blinker Control
sections.description: Lateral pause behavior during turn signals

items.title: Pause Lateral Control with Blinker
items.description: Pause lateral control with blinker when traveling below the desired speed selected.

sub_items.title: Minimum Speed to Pause Lateral Control
Post-Blinker Delay
sub_items.description: Delay before lateral control resumes after the turn signal ends.

sections.title: Torque Control
sections.description: Steering torque tuning and lateral control method

items.title: Enforce Torque Lateral Control
items.description: Enable this to enforce sunnypilot to steer with Torque lateral control.

items.title: Lateral Jerk Torque Controller
items.description: Looks ahead at planned steering to reduce sudden corrections, so the wheel moves more smoothly through turns. Works with Self-Tune and custom tuning. Thanks to @twilsonco for the implementation.

items.title: Self-Tune
items.description: Enables self-tune for Torque lateral control for platforms that do not use Torque lateral control by default.

items.title: Less Restrict Settings for Self-Tune (Beta)
items.description: Less strict settings when using Self-Tune. This allows torqued to be more forgiving when learning values.

items.title: Enable Custom Tuning
items.description: Enables custom tuning for Torque lateral control. Modifying Lateral Acceleration Factor and Friction below will override the offline values indicated in the YAML files within "opendbc/car/torque_data". The values will also be used live when "Manual Real-Time Tuning" toggle is enabled.

items.title: Manual Real-Time Tuning
items.description: Enforces the torque lateral controller to use the fixed values instead of the learned values from Self-Tune. Enabling this toggle overrides Self-Tune values.

items.title: Torque Control Tune Version
items.description: Select the version of Torque Control Tune to use.

sections.title: Lane Change
sections.description: Automatic lane change timing and behavior

items.title: Auto Lane Change by Blinker
items.description: Set a timer to delay the auto lane change operation when the blinker is used. No nudge on the steering wheel is required to auto lane change if a timer is set. Default is Nudge.
items.details: Please use caution when using this feature. Only use the blinker when traffic and road conditions permit.

items.title: Block Lane Change: Road Edge Detection
items.description: Blocks lane change when the model sees a road edge on the side you signal.

items.title: Auto Lane Change: Delay with Blind Spot
items.description: Toggle to enable a delay timer for lane changes when blind spot monitoring (BSM) detects a vehicle in your blind spot.

sections.title: Navigation
sections.description: Turn and exit desires confirmed against the navigation route, once Navigation (Alpha) is on in Developer

items.title: Navigation Turn Desires
items.description: With a route, signal for its next turn about 8 seconds ahead; on roads faster than about 45 mph (70 km/h), first move into the lane you will turn from, then signal about 15 seconds ahead, so the car can slow down in time. Farther out than about 250 m (800 ft), the blinker counts as the turn signal only once the model has seen the car in the outermost lane on the turn's side; above about 55 mph (90 km/h), if Slowing for Route Turn does not show soon after you signal, slow the car yourself (lower the set speed, or brake), or the turn is skipped. About 3 seconds before the car starts steering into the turn, it plans the turn, but only if it can still get down to turning speed by then. With openpilot longitudinal (alpha), which slows the car for the turn, it must be below 20 mph (32 km/h) and able to slow down in time, counting the speed it still gains while openpilot is speeding it up, so signal before you pull away. Route turns never start while the car's own cruise control is on. A turn that has not started by about 8 m (25 ft) before the corner, or that the car is too fast for, is skipped, and the car goes straight. From about 20 seconds before the turn, a blinker toward it never starts an automatic lane change, and a nudge changes lanes only above 20 mph, which the slowdown takes the car below about 50 m (165 ft) before the turn, so move into a turn lane before you signal.
items.details: To call a turn off, switch the blinker off, or over to the other side, before it starts; with Automatic Route Turns on, switching it off also means the car will not take that turn by itself, though it still slows for it. The gas only ends its slowdown: the car speeds up again, which usually means no turn, but if it is still slow enough and no longer speeding up, the turn starts anyway. Keep the blinker on until the turn starts: if it goes off before then, also by itself after a short signal, the turn ends, and so does its slowdown unless the car is already within about 15 m (50 ft) of the turn, so signal again. A turn that does not start leaves the car at turning speed to about 20 m (65 ft) past the corner: the gas or the other blinker before the corner ends that (not once Automatic Turn Lanes has started moving the car into a turn lane for that turn), and past it the gas overrides it only while pressed. Slowing for Route Turn does not by itself mean the turn will start. At a red light a started turn is repeated while the car waits short of the intersection, but a GPS error can still end that early, so be ready to steer when you go. Without openpilot longitudinal, route turns start only with the cruise control off, while you drive the speed yourself, below about 12 mph (20 km/h) for a right turn or 15 mph (24 km/h) for a left turn (the other way round where traffic keeps left): Tesla's cruise control speeds back up toward its set speed of 18 mph or more once the car ahead moves on, which would take the turn far too fast. Brake whenever you need to: on a Tesla that also turns steering off. A started turn keeps its slowdown through a gap in the GPS, by the distance driven, but its turn desire is not repeated without a fix, so after a stop of more than a few seconds be ready to steer; one that has not started waits for the fix. Leaving the route's road, onto a road that branches off for example, ends the route's next turn until the route is recalculated, but a road that leaves at a very shallow angle, or within about 40 m (130 ft) of the turn, can still get it. The model chooses the opening to turn into, so stay ready to steer.

items.title: Automatic Route Turns (Alpha)
items.description: Slows for each route turn, and turns right on its own (left where traffic keeps left) once slowed down and in the curb lane for a second, counted again after a lane change. Needs openpilot longitudinal (alpha). Turns across oncoming traffic wait for your blinker unless Automatic Left Turns is on; turns where the model cannot see the curb lane slow and wait for your blinker. Before an automatic turn starts, the gas pedal, the opposite blinker or disengaging calls it off until you signal for it. Switching off a blinker you had on for the turn, or a short signal that stops by itself, calls off that turn, and the car will not take it by itself either (it still slows for it), unless the car switched the blinker off itself as an openpilot lane change ended. Once a turn starts, steer to stop it (on a Tesla the brake also stops it, since it turns steering off).
items.details: Turning without signaling is illegal in most places and gives pedestrians and other drivers no warning: signal yourself where you can. The curb-lane check cannot see a bike lane behind a curb or posts, and may take a narrow painted bike lane for the curb lane, so before every automatic turn, check for cyclists on the side you are turning to, or signal. The car does not watch for pedestrians, cyclists or cross traffic, and does not reliably stop for red lights or stop signs, so watch every turn and be ready to take over.

items.title: Automatic Left Turns (Alpha)
items.description: Needs Automatic Route Turns. Also turns left on its own (right where traffic keeps left), across oncoming traffic, but only from the lane right beside a raised median or curb on that side, such as a curbed left-turn bay or the left lane of a one-way street, and only where the posted speed limit is known and 45 mph (72 km/h) or less. The model must have seen that curb right beside the car for the last 10 m (33 ft) and 1.5 seconds, with no lane change and no car in that blind spot, and the route's lane guidance must not put the turn in another lane. The turn starts only while the car is moving, at least 2 seconds before it steers across, and Turning Across Traffic chimes as it starts. Everywhere else it slows and waits for your blinker, and shows Signal for Route Turn. Change it while parked (on the comma 4 you can also switch it off while driving); with Automatic Route Turns switched on while driving, it waits until the car next stands still.
items.details: Turning Across Traffic chimes, with its own sound, at least 2 seconds before the car steers across oncoming traffic. The car does not see oncoming traffic, turn arrows, red lights or stop signs, and does not judge gaps: watch every automatic left turn and brake for oncoming traffic. On a Tesla, braking turns steering off as well as speed control, so finish the turn yourself. If the car stops within about 30 m (100 ft) of the turn before it starts, at a light, a stop sign or in a queue, the turn is left to you: the car keeps slowing for it, shows Signal for Route Turn, and turns once you signal. After the turn started, it is not repeated while the car waits or creeps, while driver monitoring warns, or in the last 2 seconds before the car steers across, and about 5 seconds after it started (or was last repeated) it is handed back to you, also if the car moves again by then: Turning Across Traffic goes away, and Signal for Route Turn shows while your blinker can still start it again. Without the blinker, a turn it refuses or hands back means the car drives straight through the intersection at about 10 mph (16 km/h), also out of a left-turn-only lane, so signal or take over when Signal for Route Turn shows. It shows from about 5 seconds before the car would steer into the turn, or as soon as the turn can no longer start by itself after that (half a second after a lane change into the bay ends, when the curb cannot be seen long enough before the turn), and once it has shown, that turn waits for your blinker; signal as soon as it shows, as a later blinker starts the turn later, and too late not at all. Painted turn lanes, center turn lanes and two-way streets have no curb beside the turn lane, so there the turn needs your blinker. The posted limit must be known, from map data or the car (where the car reads a higher limit than the map, the higher one counts), over the last 150 m (500 ft) before the turn, and driver monitoring must not be warning; its warnings show over these alerts. Quiet Mode silences their chimes. On the approach, switching off a left blinker you had on for the turn, pressing the gas, or switching on the right blinker means no automatic left turn at that intersection; the car switching the blinker off by itself as an openpilot lane change into a turn bay ends still lets the turn start by itself once the curb has been beside the car for 10 m. Frontage roads, channelized islands, curbed bus lanes and median U-turn openings can look like a turn lane to the curb check, and on one-way streets cyclists may ride on the left: watch for them. Turning without signaling is illegal in most places: signal yourself where you can. This setting is not restored from a sunnylink backup. Changing the driving model can change how curbs are seen.

items.title: Automatic Turn Lanes (Alpha)
items.description: Needs Automatic Route Turns. For a right turn (left where traffic keeps left), once the model has seen the car in the curb lane, the car moves by itself into a turn lane that opens beside it before the route turn, then turns from it. Never for left turns, across oncoming traffic, where an oncoming lane can look like a turn bay to the camera. Moving to Turn Lane chimes and shows while it moves. It moves without the blinker, which is illegal in most places, so signal yourself where you can. Change it while parked (on the comma 4 you can also switch it off while driving).
items.details: It moves once per turn, toward the turn only, into a lane the model sees open beside the car: at least 2.6 m (8.5 ft) wide, with a lane line between, no lane line beyond it, and still open 30 m (100 ft) ahead. It moves only between about 6 and 33 mph (9-54 km/h), within 150 m (490 ft) of the turn and within 50 m (165 ft) of where the car last had the curb beside it, and only where the move can end well before the turn starts, so the turn lane must be open by about 70 m (230 ft) before the turn at 20 mph, 80 m (260 ft) at 25-30 mph; a later one, and the car stays in its lane, with no automatic turn from there. It does not move with a blinker on, with a car in that blind spot, while driver monitoring warns or for 3 seconds after (its first warning has the same chime), while Block Lane Change: Road Edge Detection blocks that side, with Auto Lane Change by Blinker set to Off, or where the route's lane guidance puts the turn in another lane. Never for a left turn (right where traffic keeps left): where a median or an island ends and the road goes on two-way, the oncoming lane looks just like a curbed bay, so move into a left turn lane yourself. Nor into short bays. The model can still take a bike lane, a parking lane, a bus bay or a turn lane for an earlier street for a turn lane: watch every move. Once the move has started, only steering against it keeps the car in its lane; on a Tesla, braking turns steering off. The gas, either blinker, or a car coming up in that blind spot before the car starts moving over ends the move and its alert, but the car may still finish moving over. Near the turn, the gas, the other blinker or disengaging then calls off only the automatic turn: the car still slows to turning speed for the corner, in whichever lane it ends up, and turns only if you signal for it. Once in the turn lane, the car turns from it as from the curb lane, while the model still sees it there. Its thresholds were set without real drives: use it first on quiet streets, with full attention. This setting is not restored from a sunnylink backup.

items.title: Navigation Exit Desires (Alpha)
items.description: Near a route exit or fork with lane guidance, a light steering nudge toward it has the car keep to that side of the split. Above 20 mph with your blinker on, a nudge changes lanes instead.

items.title: Phone GPS (Alpha)
items.description: Navigation uses your iPhone's GPS in place of the comma's own, which hears little in some cars, and the comma's own GPS whenever the phone's fixes stop. Needs an iPhone app that shares its GPS over Wi-Fi, such as GPS2IP in socket mode on port 11123, kept running in the background, and the comma connected to the iPhone's Personal Hotspot.
items.details: To set it up, in GPS2IP choose Socket mode on port 11123, keep RMC (and GGA) among its NMEA sentences, turn on its background mode and start it, then connect the comma to the iPhone's Personal Hotspot. The comma connects to the phone, the hotspot's gateway, and takes its data only over that connection; another device on the hotspot could still pose as the phone, so keep the hotspot to your own devices. The navigation page's GPS details show a Phone GPS line: whether the comma is connected to the phone, how old the phone's last fix is, how long before it arrived it was taken and how accurate, and which GPS navigation uses. The phone's fixes reach the comma about a second after they were taken. The slowdown and turn timing allow for that while the iPhone's clock agrees with the comma's (the iPhone's time set automatically); if they differ, the GPS details say so, and turn commands may come about a second late. A fix taken more than 2 seconds before it arrived, held up on the way, jumping farther than the car could drive, worse than about 50 m (165 ft), or without speed or course is not used. The app must keep running: once its fixes stop, navigation goes back to the comma's own GPS within about 3 seconds. A phone in a pocket or a bag hears less: keep it where it sees the sky, such as in a dashboard mount. It works only on a comma 4, beside its own u-blox GPS.

panels.label: Cruise
panels.description: Longitudinal control, speed limits, and cruise behavior

items.title: Disengage Cruise on Accelerator Pedal
items.description: When enabled, pressing the accelerator pedal will disengage longitudinal control.

items.title: Driving Personality
items.description: Standard is recommended. In aggressive mode, sunnypilot will follow lead cars closer and be more aggressive with the gas and brake. In relaxed mode sunnypilot will stay further away from lead cars. On supported cars, you can cycle through these personalities with your steering wheel distance button.

sections.title: Speed Limits
sections.description: Speed limit detection and offset behavior

items.title: Vision
items.description: Use vision path predictions to estimate the appropriate speed to drive through turns ahead.

items.title: Map
items.description: Use map data to estimate the appropriate speed to drive through turns ahead.

panels.label: Display
panels.description: Screen brightness, timeout, and interactivity settings

sections.title: Brightness & Timeout
sections.description: Screen dimming and sleep behavior while driving

items.title: Interactivity Timeout
items.description: Apply a custom timeout for settings UI. This is the time after which settings UI closes automatically if user is not interacting with the screen.

items.title: Screen Saver
items.description: Show a screen saver when the device is offroad and idle, instead of turning the screen off.

items.title: Screen Saver Duration
items.description: How long the screen saver runs before the screen turns off.

panels.label: Visuals
panels.description: HUD overlays, alerts, and on-screen display elements

sections.title: HUD Elements
sections.description: Overlays shown on the driving screen

items.title: Show Blind Spot Warnings
items.description: Enabling this will display warnings when a vehicle is detected in your blind spot as long as your car has BSM supported.

items.title: Steering Arc
items.description: Display steering arc on the driving screen when lateral control is enabled.

items.title: Display Turn Signals
items.description: When enabled, visual turn indicators are drawn on the HUD.

items.title: Display Road Name
items.description: Displays the name of the road the car is traveling on. The OpenStreetMap database of the location must be downloaded to fetch the road name.

items.title: Standstill Timer
items.description: Show a timer on the HUD when the car is at a standstill.

items.title: Real-time Acceleration Bar
items.description: Show an indicator on the left side of the screen to display real-time vehicle acceleration and deceleration. This displays what the car is currently doing, not what the planner is requesting.

items.title: Developer UI
items.description: Display real-time parameters and metrics from various sources.

items.title: Speedometer: Always Display True Speed
items.description: For applicable vehicles, always display the true vehicle current speed from wheel speed sensors.

items.title: Speedometer: Hide from Onroad Screen
items.description: When enabled, the speedometer on the onroad screen is not displayed.

sections.title: Alerts & Extras
sections.description: Traffic light alerts and visual flair

items.title: Green Traffic Light Alert (Beta)
items.description: A chime and on-screen alert will play when the traffic light you are waiting for turns green and you have no vehicle in front of you. On-screen visual alert is only available on comma 3X. Note: This chime is only designed as a notification. It is the driver's responsibility to observe their environment and make decisions accordingly.

items.title: Lead Departure Alert (Beta)
items.description: A chime and on-screen alert will play when you are stopped, and the vehicle in front of you start moving. On-screen visual alert is only available on comma 3X. Note: This chime is only designed as a notification. It is the driver's responsibility to observe their environment and make decisions accordingly.

items.title: Tesla Rainbow Mode
items.description: Display a rainbow effect on the path the model wants to take. It does not affect driving in any way.

items.title: Enable sunnypilot
items.description: Use the sunnypilot system for adaptive cruise control and lane keep driver assistance. Your attention is required at all times to use this feature.

items.title: Enable Lane Departure Warnings
items.description: Receive alerts to steer back into the lane when your vehicle drifts over a detected lane line without a turn signal activated while driving over 31 mph (50 km/h).

items.title: Always-On Driver Monitoring
items.description: Enable driver monitoring even when sunnypilot is not engaged.

items.title: Use Metric System
items.description: Display speed in km/h instead of mph.

sections.title: Recording
sections.description: Camera and audio recording during drives

items.title: Record and Upload Driver Camera
items.description: Upload data from the driver facing camera and help improve the driver monitoring algorithm.

items.title: Record and Upload Microphone Audio
items.description: Record and store microphone audio while driving. The audio will be included in the dashcam video in comma connect.

panels.label: Device
panels.description: Device behavior, units, and recording settings

items.title: Wake Up Behavior
items.description: Controls state of the device after boot/sleep. Default: Device will boot/wake-up normally and will be ready to engage. Offroad: Device will be in Always Offroad mode after boot/wake-up.

items.title: Max Time Offroad
items.description: Device will automatically shutdown after set time once the engine is turned off. 30h is the default.

items.title: Disable Updates
items.description: When enabled, software updates will be off. This requires a reboot to take effect.

panels.label: Developer
panels.description: Debug tools, remote access, and advanced services

items.title: Enable ADB
items.description: ADB (Android Debug Bridge) allows connecting to your device over USB or over the network. See https://docs.comma.ai/how-to/connect-to-comma for more info.

items.title: sunnypilot Longitudinal Control (Alpha)
items.description: WARNING: sunnypilot longitudinal control is in alpha for this car and will disable Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB). On this car, sunnypilot defaults to the car's built-in ACC instead of sunnypilot's longitudinal control. Enable this to switch to sunnypilot longitudinal control. Enabling Experimental mode is recommended when enabling sunnypilot longitudinal control alpha. Changing this setting will restart sunnypilot if the car is powered on.

items.title: Navigation (Alpha)
items.description: Turn-by-turn navigation with a route map. Set a destination from your phone at http://<device IP>:8082, with both on your phone's hotspot or your home Wi-Fi. The page has no password, and anyone on the same Wi-Fi network can open it and change your destination, so never use the comma's own hotspot or public Wi-Fi. It is served only over Wi-Fi, never over the comma's cellular data.

sections.title: Test Maneuvers
sections.description: DANGER: enabling these maneuvers replaces normal driving behavior with deterministic test sequences. Each toggle requires explicit confirmation per write. Use only in a closed environment.

items.title: [TEST] Lateral Maneuver Mode
items.description: Replaces normal lateral control with a deterministic test sequence. NOT for road use.

items.title: [TEST] Longitudinal Maneuver Mode
items.description: Replaces normal longitudinal control with a deterministic test sequence. NOT for road use.

items.title: Show Advanced Controls
items.description: Toggle visibility of advanced sunnypilot controls. This only changes the visibility of the toggles; it does not change the actual enabled/disabled state.

items.title: GitHub Runner Service
items.description: Enables or disables the GitHub runner service.

items.title: copyparty Service
items.description: copyparty is a very capable file server, you can use it to download your routes, view your logs and even make some edits on some files from your browser. Requires you to connect to your comma locally via its IP address.

panels.label: Models
panels.description: Driving model behavior and camera calibration

sections.title: Model Behavior
sections.description: Lane desire, Blendful lane centering, and lead-vehicle awareness tuning

items.title: Blendful (Alpha)
items.description: Adds a gentle nudge toward lane center on top of the model's own steering, stronger when lane lines are clear. Yields around obstacles. Not available with the Default model.

items.title: Use Lane Turn Desires
items.description: If you are driving at 20 mph (32 km/h) or below and have your blinker on, the car will plan a turn in that direction at the nearest drivable path. This prevents situations (like at red lights) where the car might plan the wrong turn direction.

items.title: Adjust Lane Turn Speed
items.description: Set the maximum speed for lane turn desires.

items.title: Live Learning Steer Delay
items.description: Allow device to learn and adapt car's steering response time

items.title: Adjust Software Delay
items.description: Adjust the software delay when Live Learning Steer Delay is toggled off. The default software delay value is 0.2

sections.title: Lateral Control
sections.description: Neural network lateral control for supported models

items.title: Neural Network Lateral Control (NNLC)
items.description: Use a neural network for lateral control instead of the default torque controller.

items.title: Adjust Camera Offset
items.description: Virtually shift camera's perspective to move model's center to Left(+ values) or Right (- values)

items.title: Stop and Go for Manual Parking Brake (Beta)
MADS Screen Activation
items.description: Use a multi-finger press on the infotainment screen to toggle MADS. This allows the use of full MADS functionality when enabled. Selecting a higher finger count may reduce accidental activations. Note: Setting this to Off will reset your MADS settings to default.

items.title: Enforce Factory Longitudinal Control
items.description: sunnypilot will not take over control of gas and brakes. Factory Toyota longitudinal control will be used.

items.title: Stop and Go Hack (Alpha)
items.description: sunnypilot will allow some Toyota/Lexus cars to auto resume during stop and go traffic. This feature is only applicable to certain models that are able to use longitudinal control. This is an alpha feature. Use at your own risk.

items.title: TSS2 Smooth Longitudinal (Alpha)
items.description: Enable smoother longitudinal control for TSS2 vehicles. Uses a custom speed-dependent integral gain curve for smoother traffic driving.
